channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kumbetor Gold Mine Increases Gold Recovery by 3% After Modernization
item.description: The Kumbetor gold processing plant has increased its gold recovery rate by 3% following modernization efforts, according to Kumbetor Gold Company. The installation of new equipment in 2023 and 2024 has enabled additional gold extraction. Despite a decrease in the ore's gold content, the plant maintains a recovery rate above 76%.

item.title: Bolotkan Bayake uulu Appointed Governor of Batken District
item.description: Bolotkan Bayake uulu has been appointed as the head of the state administration, the akim, of Batken District in Batken Oblast. The relevant decree was signed by President Sadyr Japarov. He was previously dismissed from his prior position.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Agriculture Sector Reports Five-Year Achievements
item.description: Kyrgyzstan allocated 19.39 billion soms for irrigation development from 2021-2026, completing construction on 31 of 112 water facilities. The Ministry of Agriculture reported progress in livestock breeding, preferential lending, trade logistics, digitalization, and irrigation. A 3% interest loan program for livestock breeding was launched.

item.title: Professor Sentenced to 10 Years in Kazakhstan for Espionage
item.description: A professor has been imprisoned for 10 years in Kazakhstan on charges of espionage. The article is available in Russian. Further details regarding the case, the professor's identity, and the specific espionage charges are not provided in the source text.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Continues Development of Togolok Gold Mine with Own Resources
item.description: Construction and preparatory work are ongoing at the Togolok gold mine, which Kyrgyzstan is developing using its own funds and efforts. The project, started in 2025, includes building bridges, roads, and installing electricity. Mining operations began in spring 2026, with foundation work for the gold processing plant and construction of a waste storage facility underway.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Dismisses Concerns Over ISIS Presence in Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabiullah Mujahid has rejected concerns about the presence of ISIS in Afghanistan, stating they are unfounded. He asserted that Afghanistan will not become a base for ISIS or any other group. Mujahid added that the Taliban will not allow foreign groups to grow and threaten the country or others, urging against basing concerns on misinformation.

item.title: Arrested Nurlan Zhakupov Remains President of Water Sports Federation
item.description: Nurlan Zhakupov, the arrested chairman of the Samruk-Kazyna fund, continues to lead Kazakhstan's Water Sports Federation. The Minister of Tourism and Sports stated that the arrest has not affected the organization's work. Zhakupov was detained on November 12 on suspicion of corruption and remains president until the investigation concludes. He was appointed head of the fund in April 2023 and the federation in March 2025.

item.title: President invites Turkish companies to participate in New Tashkent construction
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has invited Turkish companies to participate in the construction of New Tashkent, citing their extensive experience and capabilities in the field. The development of toll roads, airports, and logistics centers was highlighted as a promising direction in the transport sector.

item.title: UN University regional research hub to be opened in Almaty
item.description: An agreement to establish a regional research hub of the UN University in Kazakhstan was signed between the Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the UN University. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the hub will enhance universities' potential and boost academic development in the country.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP proposes shorter workday for single parents
item.description: A Kyrgyz Member of Parliament, Dastan Bekeshev, has proposed amendments to the Labor Code allowing single parents raising children under 14 to leave work an hour earlier or arrive an hour later without a pay cut. This benefit would apply daily, regardless of the number of children or work schedule.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Spiritual Directorate Staff Check on Pilgrims Stranded in Tashkent
item.description: Staff from the Spiritual Directorate of Muslims of Kyrgyzstan visited Kyrgyz citizens unable to fly to Mecca from Tashkent. They provided explanations and confirmed 54 individuals are preparing for their pilgrimage, while others chose to return home. The Directorate is working to resolve the issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Host UFC Tournament; Minister to Announce Decision by Month-End
item.description: Kazakhstan is in negotiations to host a UFC tournament, with the Minister of Tourism and Sports stating a decision will be made by the end of the month. Talks have been ongoing since the beginning of the year. The country currently has five athletes competing in the UFC.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Expand Cooperation in Higher Education and Science
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia are broadening their collaboration in education and science. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev expressed gratitude to the Minister of Science and Higher Education for organizational efforts. The country has established branches of leading foreign universities, including Moscow State University and MGIMO.

item.title: Kumtor Gold Company Expands Fuel Storage Capacity to 19 Reservoirs
item.description: Kumtor Gold Company has increased its fuel storage reservoirs at the Balychy transit base from 9 to 19. The storage capacity has risen from 12,000 to over 32,000 cubic meters. This expansion ensures uninterrupted fuel supply to the Kumtor mine and mitigates risks. The Balychy base area is also set to double by 2025-2026 with a new office building.

item.title: Uzbek President Invites Turkish Business to Participate in New Tashkent Construction Projects
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev invited Turkish investors to participate in construction projects for "New Tashkent" and other sectors. He highlighted Uzbekistan's economic growth and attraction of over $150 billion in foreign investment since 2017. Goals include reaching $300 billion GDP by 2030 and expanding renewable energy capacity.

item.title: Arrested Head of Kazakhstan's Samruk-Kazyna to Retain Water Sports Federation Post
item.description: Nurlan Zhakupov, the arrested head of Kazakhstan's sovereign wealth fund Samruk-Kazyna, will continue to lead the Kazakhstan Water Sports Federation. A decision on his future role will be made after the investigation concludes, according to the Minister of Tourism and Sport. Samruk-Kazyna's funding for sports clubs remains unaffected.

item.title: Contraband Jewelry, Watches, and Cigarettes Seized at Tashkent Airport
item.description: Customs officers at Tashkent International Airport have intercepted three cases of undeclared goods, including jewelry, luxury watches, and a large quantity of cigarettes. The items, valued at over 306.4 million soms, were discovered in passengers' luggage and personal belongings. Investigations into these violations of customs regulations are currently underway.

item.title: Fitch Upgrades Uzbekneftegaz Outlook to Positive on Gas Price Hikes
item.description: Fitch Ratings affirmed Uzbekistan's state-owned Uzbekneftegaz's long-term rating at 'BB' and revised the outlook to 'positive' from 'stable'. The upgrade reflects a reduced relative debt burden due to significant increases in regulated natural gas prices, expected to reach $82 per 1000 cubic meters by 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports 62% Increase in Cancer Cases Detected Through Screenings
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Kazakhstan detected 3,016 cases of malignant neoplasms through cancer screenings, a 62% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Significant growth was observed in colorectal, breast, and cervical cancer detection rates. The proportion of cases detected at stage I also increased.

item.title: Putin: Russia, US, China Share Responsibility for Global Peace and Security
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia, the US, and China share a "joint responsibility for maintaining international peace and security." Speaking at the first-ever trilateral summit, he emphasized their role in preserving international law and suggested discussing global economic ties, food security, and energy. Putin noted converging interests in regional conflict resolution, including Ukraine.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Become Central Asia's Academic Hub, President Tokayev States
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced that a key goal is to transform the country into an academic hub for Central Asia. He highlighted that 18 Kazakh universities are now listed in the QS World University Rankings, and 10 higher education institutions are included in the 2027 Times Higher Education ranking. Kazakhstan also leads the region in the Global Innovation Index.

item.title: Uzbekistan Professor Sentenced to 10 Years in Kazakhstan for Espionage
item.description: An Uzbek citizen and professor, Ikboljon Koraboev, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison in Kazakhstan on charges of espionage. His family confirmed the closed-door trial and stated they were not given access to investigation materials. They are appealing the verdict and seeking his full acquittal.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan Discuss Agricultural Cooperation in Ashgabat
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, met with Turkmenistan's Minister of Agriculture, Charyyar Chetiyev, in Ashgabat. They discussed strengthening cooperation in agriculture, including developing drought-resistant grape varieties, organizing greenhouses, and joint research on fruit and vegetable cultivation.

item.title: Power Line Accident in Tajikistan Affects Fergana Valley Electricity Supply
item.description: An accident on a 500 kV power line in Tajikistan has disrupted electricity supply to Uzbekistan's Fergana Valley. The incident occurred due to adverse weather conditions causing a support structure to collapse. Emergency crews are working with Tajik organizations to restore power.

item.title: Uzbekistan Invites Turkish Companies for Joint Projects in Mining and Green Energy
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to increase gold and silver extraction and boost copper production capacity. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has invited Turkish companies to implement new joint projects in mining, deep processing of mineral resources, and green energy sectors.

item.title: Leading Universities from 11 Countries Open Branches in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has opened branches of leading higher education institutions from 11 countries, currently educating over 12,000 students with approximately 1,500 faculty members. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted this at the III Strategic Partners Forum, emphasizing international cooperation in higher education and science.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pensioners Transfer Nearly 120 Billion Tenge to Private Managers in Two Months
item.description: Kazakhstan citizens transferred 60.7 billion tenge of pension savings to private management companies in October 2026, bringing the two-month total to nearly 119 billion tenge. This represents about 40% of all funds transferred to private management since 2021.

item.title: Kazakhstan Privatizes 13 Football Clubs, Completing Process by Year-End
item.description: Thirteen football clubs in Kazakhstan have been privatized, with six more awaiting new owners. The Ministry of Tourism and Sport aims to finalize the process for the remaining clubs by the end of the year. The 'Astana' club's privatization is expected next week. This initiative follows a presidential directive to accelerate football commercialization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Retain Specialists by Partnering with Foreign Universities
item.description: President Tokayev is focusing on retaining qualified specialists, scientific achievements, and innovations in Kazakhstan by expanding cooperation with foreign universities and establishing joint research labs. The country is moving to the second stage of developing an international academic hub, emphasizing knowledge retention and talent preservation.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Vows No Mercy for Corrupt Officials
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev declared that corrupt individuals will not be shown leniency, emphasizing that those proven guilty must face legal consequences. He stated that corruption undermines public trust and hinders national development, reinforcing the principle of 'Law and Order' as a foundation for a just Kazakhstan.

item.title: South Kazakhstan University to Be Granted National Status, President Announces
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced that the South Kazakhstan University, named after Mukhtar Auezov, will be granted national status. He stated that Shymkent is intended to become a major scientific and educational hub for the southern region, joining Astana and Almaty as leading centers of science and culture.

item.title: UN Regional Research Center to Open in Almaty, Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan and the UN University have agreed to establish a regional research hub in Almaty. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated this move will enhance Kazakhstan's scientific recognition and foster collaboration with international educational and research institutions, boosting local universities.

item.title: Uch-Kurganskaya HPP Completes Major Modernization, Hydro Units Upgraded
item.description: The Uch-Kurganskaya Hydropower Plant has completed a significant modernization, with the final of four hydro units now operational. This upgrade increases the plant's total capacity by 36 megawatts, enhancing its reliability and electricity generation for Kyrgyzstan's energy system.

item.title: Gish-Kuprik Border Post in Uzbekistan Reconstructed, Capacity Increased
item.description: The Gish-Kuprik border customs post in Uzbekistan has been fully reconstructed, significantly increasing its capacity for people and transport. The post can now handle up to 100,000 people and 3,000 cars daily, with expanded infrastructure and modernized facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Athlete May Receive Prize Money Despite Asian Games Disqualification
item.description: Kazakhstan's Yasmina Toksanbayeva, disqualified from the Asian Games marathon walk, may still receive prize money if an international organization makes a favorable decision. The Minister of Tourism and Sports stated that the athlete would receive funds if the international body rules in her favor. The prize money for winners has increased to $50,000 from non-budgetary funds.

item.title: Former Afghan Minister Calls Taliban Leader's Recent Statements 'Worthy of Deep Reflection'
item.description: Omar Daudzai, a former Afghan interior minister and advisor to Ashraf Ghani, described recent statements by Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada as 'worthy of deep reflection and precise political assessment.' Daudzai, now heading a movement for Afghanistan's national salvation, urged leaders to avoid hasty reactions and consider the national interest and the country's future.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Palliative care bill for children delayed, lawmaker urges action
item.description: A lawmaker in Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber has expressed concern over the delay in a bill concerning palliative and hospice care for children with severe illnesses. The bill, mandated by a presidential decree, was due in November but has not yet been submitted. The Health Minister cited the need to adapt the draft to a newer presidential decree on palliative medical services.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches 'People's Construction' program for national development
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced Kazakhstan's 'People's Construction' program, a nationwide initiative to build kindergartens, schools, clinics, and other vital infrastructure. Tokayev stated that the program will significantly boost public welfare, foster entrepreneurship, and diversify the economy, creating new jobs and uniting the nation.

item.title: New airport planned near Ulken village in Almaty region, Kazakhstan
item.description: An airport is planned for construction in the Zhambyl district of the Almaty region, Kazakhstan. The project is part of infrastructure development related to the construction of a nuclear power plant in the same area. Local authorities confirmed the plans for the new airport.

item.title: Tajikistan Calls for Strengthening Regional Cooperation on Climate Change
item.description: At the COP31 conference, Tajikistan emphasized the need for enhanced regional and international cooperation to address climate change. The Committee for Environmental Protection highlighted climate challenges like glacier melt and water scarcity, stressing their impact on security and stability.
